title: fleet-write dispatch: apply the PR-vs-issue state-label rule to labels_add / issue_create / pr_create, and match pm labels case-insensitively
body:
domain:skills#3 · huangyiirene · session_01J8VVAj7CvjkGXvgXzd6RZ7

This card carries the half of #31148 that PR #31250 leaves open. #31148 / PR #31250 enforce the rule at `scripts/pm/label-write.mjs`. This card covers the other doors and the case gap.

## What is wrong

The rule: the six pm state labels (`pm:queue`, `pm:dispatched`, `pm:blocked`, `pm:on-hold`, `pm:awaiting-maintainer`, `needs-user-decision`) never go on a pull request, and `pm:awaiting-merge` only goes on a pull request. It is in `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md` ≈L102/L107/L194. After PR #31250, label-write refuses both. But on `main`:

1. `scripts/pm/fleet-write/dispatch.mjs` adds labels without going through label-write. It does this in a raw `labels_add`, and in `pr_create` / `issue_create` with a `labels` list. `RETIRED_LANE_REWRITE_OPS` (≈L920) already applies one label rule (retired lane aliases) to exactly these three ops, so this is the place for the PR-vs-issue rule too. The incident in #31148 (cloud PR #3680) was written by `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, the account behind both doors, so the record does not show which door it went through.
2. The match is case-sensitive, in both `refuseTwoStates` and the new #31250 refusal. GitHub label names match case-insensitively, so adding `Needs-User-Decision` applies the existing `needs-user-decision` label and gets past both checks.

## Expected

- dispatch.mjs refuses, before any write and with the rule quoted: a state label in `labels_add` on a pull request (or in `pr_create`'s labels), and `pm:awaiting-merge` in `labels_add` on an issue (or in `issue_create`'s labels). Reuse label-write's predicate rather than restating it.
- Both doors compare pm labels case-insensitively (`refuseTwoStates` included).
- Removals are never refused. One self-test case per door and direction.

## Evidence

Contract review on PR #31250, S1 and N1.
